content: Common Side Effects The following side effects have been reported with the use of this medication: back pain (7%), dizziness (7%), abdominal pain (6%), dyspepsia (6%), vomiting (6%), and fatigue (5%). Other potential adverse effects include adrenal suppression, amnesia, anaphylactic reactions, benign intracranial hypertension, diarrhea, facial edema, fever, flu-like syndrome, gastrointestinal irritation, hypokalemia, increased appetite, insomnia, migraine, nervousness, pharyngitis, rash, xerostomia (dry mouth), weight gain, rectal bleeding, peripheral edema, muscle cramps or spasms, mood swings, and increased blood pressure. Hypersensitivity reactions have also been documented. Chronic Use and Systemic Effects When used chronically, systemic effects such as hypercorticism and adrenal suppression may occur. Glucocorticosteroids, including budesonide, can suppress the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis response to stress. Patients undergoing surgery or other stress-inducing situations may require supplementation with systemic glucocorticosteroids. Caution is advised when transitioning patients from glucocorticosteroids with higher systemic effects to those with lower systemic effects (e.g., budesonide). Monitor for symptoms of steroid withdrawal, including acute adrenal suppression or benign intracranial hypertension. Infection Risk Drugs that suppress the immune system, such as budesonide, may increase the risk of infections. Patients who have not had certain infections (e.g., chickenpox, measles) may experience more severe or even fatal infections. Liver Function and Systemic Availability Reduced liver function can impair the elimination of glucocorticosteroids. Increased systemic availability of oral budesonide has been observed in patients with liver cirrhosis. Consider discontinuing budesonide in patients with moderate-to-severe liver disease. Precautions for Specific Conditions Exercise caution in patients with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, osteoporosis, peptic ulcer disease, glaucoma, cataracts, or other conditions where glucocorticosteroids may have undesirable effects. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding Available data from case series, epidemiological studies, and reviews have not identified a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes with oral budesonide use during pregnancy. Breastfeeding is not expected to result in significant exposure to the infant. However, no lactation studies have been conducted, and there is limited information on the effects on infants or milk production. One study has reported the presence of budesonide in human milk following maternal inhalation. Routine monitoring of linear growth in infants is recommended with chronic use of budesonide in nursing mothers. Grapefruit Juice Interaction Avoid consuming grapefruit juice during treatment, as it may interfere with the medication's metabolism. Missed Dose Instructions If a dose is missed, take the prescribed dose at the next scheduled time. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Storage Instructions Store the medication at room temperature, away from heat and open flames, as it is flammable. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Usage Instructions This medication is used to treat symptoms of ulcerative colitis by reducing inflammation. It is applied rectally as a foam, typically twice daily (morning and evening) for the first two weeks, then once daily in the evening for the next four weeks. Use the enclosed applicator to administer the foam, following the provided instructions. Warm the canister in your hands and shake it well before use. Avoid smoking during and immediately after application, as the medication is flammable. Wash your hands thoroughly after use. Withdrawal Symptoms If you are transitioning from another oral corticosteroid (e.g., prednisone), do not stop taking it abruptly unless directed by your doctor. Sudden discontinuation may worsen conditions such as asthma or allergies and cause withdrawal symptoms, including weakness, weight loss, nausea, muscle pain, headache, fatigue, and dizziness. Your doctor may gradually reduce the dose of your previous medication to prevent withdrawal. Side Effects and Risks Nausea may occur. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, leading to systemic corticosteroid side effects, which are more likely in children or long-term users. Budesonide may lower your ability to fight infections, increasing the risk of serious or fatal infections or worsening existing infections. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any concerning symptoms. Precautions Before using budesonide, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it or have other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Long-term use of corticosteroids may impair your body’s ability to respond to physical stress. Budesonide may mask signs of infection, making you more susceptible to new infections or worsening existing ones. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections (e.g., chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, flu). Inform your healthcare provider that you are using budesonide before receiving any vaccinations. Drug Interactions Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. Overdose If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S.). Lifestyle Recommendations To reduce the risk of bone loss (osteoporosis) during long-term corticosteroid treatment, engage in weight-bearing exercise, ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake, avoid smoking, and limit alcohol consumption. Important Notes This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
